## ਸਾਫ਼ਟਵੇਅਰ ਇੰਜੀਨੀਅਰ ਦੇ ਤਕਨੀਕੀ ਹੁਨਰਾਂ ਦਾ ਮੁਲਾਂਕਣ

ਉਮੀਦਵਾਰ ਨੂੰ ਅਹੁਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਮੇਲ ਖਾਂਦਾ ਇੱਕ ਪ੍ਰੋਗਰਾਮ ਬਣਾਉਣ ਜਾਂ ਸੁਧਾਰਨ ਦਾ ਕੰਮ ਦਿਓ। ਉਸ ਦਾ ਹੱਲ, ਉਸ ਵੱਲੋਂ ਕੀਤੀ ਜਾਂਚ ਅਤੇ ਆਪਣੇ ਫ਼ੈਸਲਿਆਂ ਲਈ ਦਿੱਤੇ ਕਾਰਨ ਵੇਖ ਕੇ ਹਰੇਕ ਹੁਨਰ ਨੂੰ ੧ ਤੋਂ ੪ ਅੰਕ ਦਿਓ।

| ਹੁਨਰ | ੧ ਅੰਕ | ੨ ਅੰਕ | ੩ ਅੰਕ | ੪ ਅੰਕ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ਸਮੱਸਿਆ ਦੀ ਸਮਝ | ਮੁੱਖ ਲੋੜ ਸਮਝਣ ਵਿੱਚ ਚੂਕਦਾ ਹੈ। | ਮਦਦ ਨਾਲ ਮੁੱਖ ਲੋੜ ਅਤੇ ਆਮ ਹਾਲਤ ਪਛਾਣਦਾ ਹੈ। | ਸਵਾਲ ਪੁੱਛ ਕੇ ਲੋੜਾਂ, ਪਾਬੰਦੀਆਂ ਅਤੇ ਸਫਲਤਾ ਦੀਆਂ ਸ਼ਰਤਾਂ ਸਪਸ਼ਟ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ। | ਜਿੱਥੇ ਇੱਕ ਲੋੜ ਦੇ ਦੋ ਅਰਥ ਨਿਕਲਦੇ ਹਨ, ਉੱਥੇ ਮਿਸਾਲ ਦੇ ਕੇ ਫ਼ਰਕ ਸਮਝਾਉਂਦਾ ਅਤੇ ਸਹੀ ਅਰਥ ਦੀ ਪੁਸ਼ਟੀ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ। |
| ਹੱਲ ਦੀ ਸ਼ੁੱਧਤਾ | ਆਮ ਹਾਲਤ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੀ ਨਤੀਜਾ ਗ਼ਲਤ ਆਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ। | ਆਮ ਹਾਲਤ ਵਿੱਚ ਹੱਲ ਚੱਲਦਾ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਕਿਸੇ ਦੱਸੀ ਹੋਈ ਸ਼ਰਤ ਉੱਤੇ ਖਰਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਉਤਰਦਾ। | ਆਮ ਅਤੇ ਹੱਦੀ ਹਾਲਤਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਾਰੀਆਂ ਦੱਸੀਆਂ ਸ਼ਰਤਾਂ ਪੂਰੀਆਂ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ। | ਸਮਝਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਹੱਲ ਮਨਜ਼ੂਰਸ਼ੁਦਾ ਦਾਇਰੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਹੀ ਨਤੀਜਾ ਕਿਉਂ ਦਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਅਣਮਨਜ਼ੂਰ ਮੁੱਲਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਮਿੱਥੇ ਢੰਗ ਨਾਲ ਸੰਭਾਲਦਾ ਹੈ। |
| ਕੋਡ ਦੀ ਬਣਤਰ ਅਤੇ ਪੜ੍ਹਨਯੋਗਤਾ | ਅਸਪਸ਼ਟ ਨਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਰਲੀ ਹੋਈ ਕਾਰਜਵਿਧੀ ਕਾਰਨ ਕੋਡ ਸਮਝਣਾ ਔਖਾ ਹੈ। | ਨਾਂ ਸਮਝ ਆਉਂਦੇ ਹਨ, ਪਰ ਇੱਕੋ ਤਬਦੀਲੀ ਕਈ ਥਾਵਾਂ ਉੱਤੇ ਕਰਨੀ ਪੈਂਦੀ ਹੈ। | ਅਰਥਪੂਰਨ ਨਾਂ ਵਰਤਦਾ ਹੈ, ਵੱਖਰੇ ਕੰਮ ਵੱਖ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਬੇਲੋੜੀ ਦੁਹਰਾਈ ਤੋਂ ਬਚਦਾ ਹੈ। | ਇੱਕ ਨਵੀਂ ਲੋੜ ਲਾਗੂ ਕਰਕੇ ਦਿਖਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਤਬਦੀਲੀ ਸਬੰਧਤ ਹਿੱਸੇ ਤੱਕ ਸੀਮਤ ਰਹਿੰਦੀ ਹੈ। |
| ਜਾਂਚ ਅਤੇ ਖ਼ਰਾਬੀ ਦਾ ਨਿਦਾਨ | ਨਤੀਜਾ ਪਰਖੇ ਬਿਨਾਂ ਕੰਮ ਪੂਰਾ ਮੰਨ ਲੈਂਦਾ ਹੈ। | ਆਮ ਹਾਲਤ ਪਰਖਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਸੰਕੇਤ ਮਿਲਣ ਉੱਤੇ ਖ਼ਰਾਬੀ ਲੱਭਦਾ ਹੈ। | ਆਮ ਅਤੇ ਹੱਦੀ ਹਾਲਤਾਂ ਪਰਖਦਾ ਹੈ, ਖ਼ਰਾਬੀ ਦੁਹਰਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਉਸ ਦਾ ਕਾਰਨ ਲੱਭਦਾ ਹੈ। | ਅਜਿਹੀ ਜਾਂਚ ਲਿਖਦਾ ਹੈ ਜੋ ਸੁਧਾਰ ਤੋਂ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਖ਼ਰਾਬੀ ਫੜਦੀ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਸੁਧਾਰ ਤੋਂ ਬਾਅਦ ਸਫਲ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ। |
| ਕਾਰਗੁਜ਼ਾਰੀ ਅਤੇ ਸਰੋਤਾਂ ਦੀ ਵਰਤੋਂ | ਸਮਝਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਕਦਾ ਕਿ ਦਿੱਤੇ ਅੰਕੜਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਮਾਤਰਾ ਵਧਣ ਨਾਲ ਹੱਲ ਉੱਤੇ ਕੀ ਅਸਰ ਪਵੇਗਾ। | ਅੰਦਾਜ਼ਾ ਲਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਕਿਹੜਾ ਹਿੱਸਾ ਹੌਲਾ ਪੈ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ। | ਸਮਝਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਅੰਕੜੇ ਵਧਣ ਨਾਲ ਸਮੇਂ ਅਤੇ ਮੈਮਰੀ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਕਿਵੇਂ ਬਦਲਦੀ ਹੈ। | ਅਸਲ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਨਾਲ ਮੇਲ ਖਾਂਦੇ ਅੰਕੜਿਆਂ ਉੱਤੇ ਹੱਲ ਮਾਪਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਮਾਪਾਂ ਦੇ ਆਧਾਰ ਉੱਤੇ ਸੁਧਾਰ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਬਾਰੇ ਫ਼ੈਸਲਾ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ। |

**ਕੁੱਲ ਅੰਕ ੨੦ ਹਨ।** ਹਰੇਕ ਹੁਨਰ ਲਈ ਉਹ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਉੱਚਾ ਪੱਧਰ ਚੁਣੋ ਜਿਸ ਦਾ ਕੰਮ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਪਸ਼ਟ ਸਬੂਤ ਮਿਲਿਆ ਹੋਵੇ। ਅੰਕ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਇੱਕ ਠੋਸ ਮਿਸਾਲ ਦਰਜ ਕਰੋ। ਜੇ ਕੰਮ ਵਿੱਚ ਕੋਈ ਹੁਨਰ ਦਿਖਾਉਣ ਦਾ ਮੌਕਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਮਿਲਿਆ, ਤਾਂ ਕੁੱਲ ਅੰਕ ਕੱਢਣ ਤੋਂ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਉਸ ਹੁਨਰ ਲਈ ਇੱਕ ਛੋਟਾ ਪੂਰਕ ਕੰਮ ਦਿਓ।

“Adventist” here refers to the Seventh-day Adventist Church. Adventists and Baptists both teach salvation by grace through faith in Jesus Christ and practice baptism by immersion for people who profess faith. Baptist beliefs vary across congregations, but several differences are common.

- [Worship] Adventists observe the Sabbath from Friday sunset to Saturday sunset. Most Baptists gather for worship on Sunday.
- [Authority] Both traditions regard the Bible as their highest authority. Adventists also recognize a prophetic gift in the ministry of Ellen G. White. Baptists generally give her writings no special authority.
- [Death and judgment] Adventists teach that the dead are unconscious until the resurrection and that Christ began a phase of heavenly judgment in 1844. Many Baptists believe that believers are with Christ immediately after death, and Baptists generally do not share the Adventist teaching about 1844.
- [Church governance] Adventist congregations belong to a worldwide representative organization. Baptist congregations typically govern themselves, though many cooperate through associations or conventions.
- [Health practices] Adventist teaching encourages vegetarianism and calls for abstinence from alcohol and tobacco. Baptist practices vary, and vegetarianism is generally a matter of personal choice.

A GNSS timestamp tells you when your Android phone used navigation satellites to figure out where it was. To get one in an app, turn on Location and grant the app precise location access. In the app’s code, use `LocationManager` to request updates from `GPS_PROVIDER`. Go outside with a clear view of the sky and wait for a new location update. When it arrives, call `location.getTime()` to read the time of that fix in milliseconds since January 1, 1970, at midnight UTC.

nell arden  
glass artist and educator  
adelaide, south australia  
nell.arden@example.com

## artist profile

i make blown and kiln-formed glass in adelaide. my work often starts with an ordinary local object, such as a louvre pulled from a kitchen window or a preserving jar with a tide mark halfway up its side. i am interested in the evidence that someone has handled a thing for years. alongside my exhibition practice, i make tableware for small restaurants, develop architectural glass with local tradespeople, and teach adults who are coming to a workshop for the first time. i have worked in shared hot shops for twelve years and can lead a production team, assist another maker, or take a commission from its first drawing through installation.

## professional experience

### independent glass artist | arden glass studio | adelaide | 2018 to present

- design and produce a small range of drinking glasses, bowls, and carafes. the first carafe had a round body that slipped in a wet hand. after trying it during a busy lunch service, i moved the widest point down and added a shallow thumb rest. that revised shape has stayed in production for six years.
- manage commissions from initial conversation to delivery. i provide drawings, dimensions, colour samples, a written estimate, and a schedule. for pieces destined for older houses, i visit the site to see the surrounding materials and how the light changes over the course of an afternoon.
- hire assistants for production days and agree on roles before the furnace work begins. i keep a sample of each approved design on the bench so that the team can check proportions between pieces. each assistant receives a making credit in the studio record.
- photograph finished pieces and maintain an archive of recipes, firing records, invoices, packing diagrams, and installation photographs. the archive proved its worth when a restaurant ordered replacements four years after its first purchase and still had only one original glass to measure.

### glassblower and workshop coordinator | west yard glassworks | bowden | 2014 to 2018

- assisted three resident makers with production tableware and exhibition pieces. my responsibilities grew from preparing tools and finishing bases to blowing matched forms, scheduling annealer space, and supervising the final coldworking of each order.
- reorganised the sample shelves after two nearly identical blues became difficult to distinguish under workshop lighting. i made a numbered set of tiles with both thin and thick sections, which allowed makers to compare how each colour would read at the intended wall thickness.
- coordinated public demonstrations during open studio weekends. i gave visitors a clear view of the bench, described what the team was doing during natural pauses, and saved a finished example for people to handle once they stepped away from the working area.

## selected exhibitions

### what the window kept | solo exhibition | hinge room gallery | port adelaide | 2025

made fourteen shallow glass panels from impressions of patterned windows in houses around the port. residents chose the windows and told me where each one had been fitted. one woman remembered recognising her father's work shirt through the bathroom glass long before she could see his face. with her permission, a short excerpt from that conversation accompanied the panel. the works hung slightly forward of the wall so their patterns cast a second image that shifted as visitors moved through the room.

### table for the late shift | two-person exhibition | corner return project space | thebarton | 2023

worked with a furniture maker to build a table setting from interviews with bakers, cleaners, and hospital staff about the meal they ate after work. i contributed nine drinking vessels and three low bowls. a baker described wrapping both hands around a glass of milk at dawn. her account led to the heaviest glass in the group, with a broad base and a band of fine wheel cuts where her fingertips would settle.

## selected commissions

### dining room glassware | little quince dining room | goodwood | 2024

produced sixty stackable water glasses for a thirty-seat dining room. during the trial, the floor staff pointed out that the original glasses nested too deeply and were hard to separate when warm from the dishwasher. i adjusted the taper and delivered a second trial set before making the full order. the restaurant retained both trial shapes for staff training, and i supplied a dimensioned drawing for future orders.

### sidelight for a family home | private commission | prospect | 2022

designed a set of textured panels for an entrance facing a narrow footpath. the owners wanted afternoon light in the hall and privacy at street level. i made full-size paper studies and four glass samples, which we viewed from the pavement and from inside the house. a licensed glazier handled the final installation. i returned several weeks later to photograph the finished entrance at the hour when the family usually arrived home.

## teaching and mentoring

### sessional tutor | south yard craft school | adelaide | 2019 to present

teach introductory kiln-forming and coldworking in groups of six. each student begins with a small transparent tile, then draws the outline of its shadow at several distances from a sheet of paper. this gives the group a shared reference when we discuss edges, surface finish, and thickness. in the final session, students choose one piece to finish and explain which decisions they would repeat. i keep examples of my own unsuccessful tests in the classroom because a visible bubble or uneven edge gives us something specific to discuss.

## education and training

- advanced diploma in studio glass, southern workshop school of art, adelaide, 2013. my final project examined the repeated shapes of pressed pantry glass and included a set of handblown measures for dry ingredients.
- professional placement in coldworking and finishing, north court glass studio, 2014. completed supervised work in wheel cutting, grinding, polishing, and the preparation of stable bases for irregular vessels.

## technical skills

free blowing, mould blowing, kiln forming, slump mould preparation, diamond wheel cutting, sandblasting, edge finishing, and polishing. experienced in costing short production runs and packing fragile works for road freight. comfortable working from a measured drawing or developing a form at the bench with another maker. i maintain a handling sheet for each exhibition series so gallery staff can identify the lifting points, preferred orientation, and packing position of every piece.

*Inheritance and captivity*

Raymond III became count of Tripoli in 1152 after the Assassins killed his father Raymond II outside the gates of Tripoli. Raymond was about twelve years old. His mother Hodierna governed the county until he came of age. In 1164 he joined other Christian rulers in an attempt to relieve the fortress of Harim. The army suffered a crushing defeat and Nur ad-Din took Raymond prisoner. He spent nearly nine years in captivity before securing his release in 1173 through the payment of a large ransom. His subsequent marriage to Eschiva of Bures made him prince of Galilee and gave him a direct interest in the defense of Tiberias.

*Regent of Jerusalem*

King Amalric of Jerusalem died in 1174 while his son Baldwin IV was still a minor. Raymond claimed the regency as a close relative of the young king. He governed until Baldwin came of age in 1176. The question of who would succeed Baldwin remained urgent because the king suffered from leprosy. In 1180 Baldwin arranged for his sister Sibylla to marry Guy of Lusignan. The marriage gave Guy a claim to political power that brought him into rivalry with Raymond. Baldwin later had Sibylla’s young son from her first marriage crowned as Baldwin V. Raymond again became regent and governed after Baldwin IV died. The death of Baldwin V in 1186 brought this arrangement to an end. Sibylla secured the crown and had Guy crowned alongside her.

*The road to Hattin*

Raymond withdrew to Tiberias and made a separate truce with Saladin. The danger of division became apparent in 1187 when a Muslim force passed through Raymond’s territory and defeated a Christian force at the Springs of Cresson. Raymond subsequently reconciled with Guy. When Saladin attacked Tiberias that summer Eschiva took refuge in its citadel. Although his own wife was under siege Raymond advised the king to keep the army near the water at Sephoria. He argued that losing Tiberias would be less damaging than risking the kingdom’s field army on a march to relieve it.

*Defeat and succession*

Guy ultimately ordered the advance. Saladin’s forces harassed the thirsty army and defeated it at the Horns of Hattin on 4 July 1187. Raymond escaped with a small group while Guy and many other nobles fell into captivity. Eschiva subsequently surrendered the citadel. Raymond returned to Tripoli and died there later that year. He had no children and left the county to his godson Raymond of Antioch.
